topic: Ecosystem difficulty relief and Ancient Heartwood health progression
currentUserGoal: Make the ecosystem game less punishing after the scripted first loss, strengthen player progression, and add a permanent way to increase the field's health.
workCompleted: Preserved the intentionally unwinnable Run 1 onboarding while reducing post-collapse Scourge base demand by roughly 15-20 percent across progression tiers.
Lengthened the post-collapse Scourge ramps so automation and field growth have more time to come online before demand accelerates.
Raised base manual Care from 5.2 to 6.0 per full-power touch.
Raised the permanent manual-touch bonus from 1 percent to 1.5 percent per Memory investment and made the displayed percentage retain half-percent precision.
Raised helper throughput scaling from 12 percent to 15 percent per rank, producing materially shorter helper cycle cooldowns.
Added Ancient Heartwood as a ten-rank Field Vitality Memory. Each rank adds 15 maximum Ancient HP to future fields, from 100 base HP to a 250 HP cap.
Added Heartwood pricing, purchase behavior, save normalization, future-run application, debug unlock behavior, Memory Web presentation, detail copy, and semantic controls.
Placed the new Heartwood branch beside Field Heir without crossed connectors, overlapping nodes, or clipped default framing.
Reset the local browser playtest to a clean Run 1 after verification.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 185 Vitest tests across 23 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Targeted ecosystem system, Memory Web, and save verification passed: 60 tests across 3 files.
The deterministic full-rate Run 2 benchmark now lasts 57.0 seconds, begins at 5.55 Scourge Care per second, buys its first sprinkler at 5.32 seconds, and still has full HP at that purchase.
Run 1 still waits for the first touch and then collapses on the first 250 ms production tick, including with debug-unlocked Memories.
Strict Memory Web geometry checks passed with 55 nodes: no connector crossings, node overlaps, blocked branches, or narrow shared-node branch angles.
Browser verification confirmed an 8-Grass-Touch Heartwood purchase, +15 maximum HP, +1.5 percent additional manual power, and a 115/115 HP Run 2.
Desktop and 390x844 browser layouts showed readable Heartwood node and detail presentation with no browser warnings or errors.
git diff --check passed apart from normal Windows LF-to-CRLF notices.

gitStatus.expectedAfterCommit: Balance and Heartwood checkpoint committed locally; master is expected to be one commit ahead of origin/master and has not been pushed or deployed.

knownIssues: The new balance curve is deterministic and browser-verified but still needs the user's hands-on progression test across several consecutive runs.
Ancient Heartwood applies to newly created fields; an already active or ended field intentionally retains the max HP stored in that run snapshot.
Late-game Scourge tiers were softened proportionally but have not yet received a long-form real-player balance pass.
nextRecommendedSteps: Play Runs 2-5 normally and note whether each loss feels earned, whether Heartwood competes fairly with throughput Memories, and where the next difficulty wall appears.
Tune Heartwood costs or later Scourge tiers from hands-on timing instead of making another broad blind adjustment.
Consider a later regeneration or damage-resistance branch only if raw maximum HP does not create enough build variety.
Push and deploy only when the user requests the next live release.
doNotRevert: Do not weaken the scripted Run 1 collapse; the requested difficulty relief begins with Run 2.
Do not remove heartwoodRank from v1 permanent-state normalization; missing legacy values must continue defaulting to zero.
Do not move Heartwood back to the clipped far-left position or introduce Memory Web connector crossings.
Do not touch docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md without explicit user direction.
